hypothesis: name resolution / type checking / borrow checking as census oracle for Rust facts

measurement.oracle: rust-analyzer 1.90.0 (official toolchain component, same distribution as rustc 1.90.0; `rustup component add rust-analyzer`), `rust-analyzer scip .` over the workspace: 92 documents, 99,321 occurrences, 53 s, 9.2 MB
measurement.method: minimal SCIP protobuf decoder (measurement only); a CALL site counts as oracle-resolvable when a non-local, non-definition callable occurrence (descriptor ending '().') lies on its line at or after its column -- a same-line heuristic, not a proof of the exact callee
measurement.stable_rustc_outputs: no machine-readable name-resolution output on stable rustc 1.90 (-Zunpretty and save-analysis are nightly-only or removed)

finding: P0 CALL coverage is 100% unresolved in Atlas and ~89% resolvable by compiler-grade resolution; the SCIP symbols rust-analyzer emits share the descriptor shape Atlas absorbed in G66 (`rust-analyzer cargo core 0.1.0 atlas/write().` vs Atlas `core atlas/write().`)

decision.EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY: compiler-grade Rust resolution through the pinned toolchain's rust-analyzer as an oracle / independent engine (a bootstrap boundary, never a hidden runtime dependency: absent tool -> engine absent, recorded)
REFERENCE_ONLY: rustc_resolve / rustc_hir_typeck / borrow checker internals (far too large to absorb; the oracle exposes their results)
decision.next: G74 (P0): import the SCIP oracle into the census -- resolve CALL records and add a second independent engine, with version pinning and a content-keyed cache

extinction.runtime_dependency: none (the oracle is the installed toolchain, not this source)
